torano--exodus-1959.description: Charlie Toraño created Exodus 1959, first released in 2001, to mark the year many Cuban tobacco families, his own among them, left the island after nationalization. A Nicaraguan Habano wrapper covers a Honduran binder and long filler from the Dominican Republic, Honduras, Mexico, Nicaragua and Costa Rica. Box-pressed and creamy-sweet, it shifts in flavor and strength as it burns.

sources.title: Cigar Place – Toraño Exodus 1959
Neptune Cigar – Toraño Exodus 1959 Robusto
Cigar Dojo – Toraño Exodus (2016) review, with Exodus history

torano--exodus-1959-50-years.description: Released for the fiftieth anniversary of the 1959 Cuban revolution and the exodus that followed, this Toraño blend is made in Nicaragua from Estelí and Pueblo Nuevo long filler under a Honduran binder and a mottled Brazilian Arapiraca maduro wrapper. Espresso, cocoa and gingerbread-like spice lead, turning towards sweet wood, cinnamon and molasses.

sources.title: Famous Smoke Shop – Carlos Toraño Exodus 1959 50 Years
Cigar Place – Exodus 1959 50 Years Box Press Robusto

torano--exodus-1959-silver.description: A follow-up to the original Exodus 1959, the Silver pairs a Criollo wrapper with a Costa Rican binder and a filler of Costa Rican, Honduran and Mexican tobacco, a gentler and more traditional build than many dense Nicaraguan puros. Toasted nuts, hickory-like wood and a hint of nutmeg define a smooth smoke with little spice.

sources.title: Cigar Place – Toraño Exodus 1959 Silver
Cigar Inspector – Exodus 1959 Silver Edition Corona Grande reviews
Cigar Dojo – Toraño Exodus (2016) review, with Exodus history

torano--exodus-1959-gold.description: The Exodus Gold 1959 is a box-pressed Toraño blend made in Nicaragua, with a Habana 2000 wrapper over a Honduran binder and a multi-country long filler. Black pepper and cedar open over chocolate and roasting nuts; the pepper then recedes as a creamy, sweet chocolate takes over, and the cedar hardens into a woody close.

thirds.notes: Prominent black pepper and deepening cedar, with chocolate behind and nuts roasting as the cigar warms.
Chocolate sweetness deepens, the pepper falls back, and a creamy texture brings out a rich nuttiness.
The pepper fades, the cedar turns harder and woodier, and chocolate melts into dark, nutty tobacco.

sources.title: Cigars International – Toraño Exodus Gold 1959
Kaplowitz – Carlos Toraño Exodus 1959 Gold review

torano--1916-cameroon.description: Named for 1916, the year Don Santiago Toraño began in Cuban tobacco, this line is hand-made in Estelí with a Nicaraguan-grown Cameroon wrapper, a Nicaraguan binder and Cuban-seed Nicaraguan and Honduran filler. An easygoing smoke of wood, earth and a dry, peppery spice, for an hour that asks for little attention.

thirds.notes: A peppery tingle and woody sweetness over an earthy base, with a dry finish after each draw.
The pepper eases and a mild, creamy woodiness takes over before the spice returns late in the third.
Wood and light pepper hold to the end as the deeper, earthy notes come back.

sources.title: Cigar Place – Toraño 1916 Cameroon
Cigar Inspector – Carlos Toraño 1916 Cameroon Robusto review
Cigar Obsession – Carlos Toraño 1916 Cameroon Robusto review
Cigars International – Staff review, Toraño 1916 Cameroon

torano--loyal.description: Introduced at the 2011 IPCPR show, Toraño Loyal sits under a creamy-brown Ecuadorian Sumatra wrapper with a binder of Nicaraguan and Dominican tobacco. It is an approachable, densely packed smoke: mild wood and grass with a touch of salt at first, then caramel, semi-sweet chocolate and leather, ending on sweet oak.

thirds.notes: Mild wood and grassy notes with a little salt, minimal spice and a short finish.
Hints of caramel, semi-sweet chocolate and leather join; the retrohale adds earth and wood.
A semi-sweet smoke with fruity, sweet oak and a medium finish that fades quickly.

sources.title: Cigar Inspector – Toraño Loyal Robusto review
Cigar Press – Toraño Cigars Loyal

torano--master.description: Toraño Master was developed by Charlie Toraño with master roller Felipe Sosa and is made in Nicaragua, with an Ecuadorian wrapper over Nicaraguan binder and filler. Hazelnut and fresh-roasted coffee lead, with gingerbread and nutmeg spice; the nuttiness grows midway, and salt and pepper sharpen the final third.

thirds.notes: Hazelnut over a starchy base, with fresh-roasted coffee arriving after the first inch.
The nuttiness comes forward while gingerbread and nutmeg soften into the background.
Spice becomes more pronounced, with salt and pepper felt on the mid-palate.

sources.title: Mike's Cigars – Carlos Toraño Master BFC
Cigar Inspector – Toraño Master Churchill review

torano--master-habano-maduro.description: The maduro version of Toraño Master, again made with master roller Felipe Sosa, uses a dark Nicaraguan-grown Habano maduro wrapper. Medium in strength but full in flavor, it opens with sweet earth, pepper and leather, adds a soft, semi-sweet cocoa midway, and finishes on pepper as the cocoa fades.

thirds.notes: Thick, sweet earth with pepper, leather and an oily texture; the finish is short and clean.
A soft, semi-sweet cocoa joins, the earth turns very smooth and the finish lengthens.
The cocoa fades and pepper comes through on the draw, with no rise in strength.

sources.title: Cigar Inspector – Toraño Master Maduro release
Cigar Obsession – Toraño Master Maduro Robusto review

torano--reserva-decadencia.description: Toraño Reserva Decadencia shares its blend with the Reserva Selecta, a long filler of Dominican, Honduran and Nicaraguan tobacco, but the leaf rests in French oak barrels that once held a chocolate port. Hand-made in Honduras, it smokes mild and creamy, with cocoa and a port-like sweetness over a gentle spice.

thirds.notes: Mild, classic tobacco with a gentle spice and a port-like finish.
The flavors build in balance; the spice grows and the port note lingers longer.
The port recedes and rich, creamy tobacco carries a long, clean finish.

sources.title: Cigars International – Toraño Reserva Decadencia
C.Gars Ltd – Toraño Reserva Decadencia Robusto review

torano--virtuoso.description: Virtuoso is the first Toraño cigar under a sun-grown wrapper from the family's own farm in Nuevo Pueblo, Nicaragua, over a Honduran binder and filler of Nicaraguan, Honduran and Panamanian tobacco. Full-bodied from the first inch, it layers earth, cream, cocoa and espresso, then nuts and honey, and gains strength in the last third.

thirds.notes: Earth and red pepper first, then a light, whipped-cream sweetness with cocoa, espresso and leather.
Cashew, almond and hazelnut arrive, cocoa and espresso deepen, and honey appears at the halfway mark.
Each note builds on the last, sweetness and spice rising as the strength climbs.

sources.title: Cigar Place – Toraño Virtuoso
Kohnhed – Carlos Toraño Virtuoso review

torano--captiva.description: Named for the island off Florida's southwest coast where Charlie Toraño spends his summers, Captiva was the first release to carry his name. An oily Ecuadorian Habano wrapper covers an all-Nicaraguan core, made in Nicaragua. Cocoa, dark chocolate and coffee lead with a floral note and pepper, softening midway before pepper and wood close.

thirds.notes: Cocoa and dark chocolate with a little coffee and wood, a perfumed floral retrohale and tingling pepper.
Rounder chocolate joins cocoa and coffee, with occasional white pepper and a graham-like sweetness.
The floral and coffee notes recede, leaving pepper, cream and wood.

sources.title: Cigar.com – Toraño Captiva
Holt's – Toraño Captiva
Blind Man's Puff – Toraño Captiva Robusto review
